lesson.title: Begin with care
lesson.text: Ask who benefits, who chooses, and what helps life continue. Ethical coherence gives each world room to differ.
lesson.prompt: Notice a design that gives someone a choice.

name: HALO
description: A peaceful threshold and protective boundaries

lesson.title: A protective threshold
lesson.text: Protection begins with observation, space, and a gentle response. HALO explores boundaries that protect without domination.
lesson.prompt: Find a boundary that protects without trapping.

lesson.title: Room to settle
lesson.text: Rest, shade, quiet and predictable paths can make a place easier to inhabit. Regulation begins with room to pause.
lesson.prompt: Choose a quiet place to pause before exploring.

lesson.title: Follow the water
lesson.text: Supply, use, recovery and discharge are different stages. A circulating loop needs appropriate treatment; circulation alone does not make water safe.
lesson.prompt: Trace a water path and identify where its uses must stay separate.

lesson.title: Grow a living garden
lesson.text: Food plants, native habitat, pollinators, shade and soil belong in the same design. A proposed planting becomes evidence only after field observation.
lesson.prompt: Observe one relationship between a plant and another living thing.

lesson.title: Connections need room
lesson.text: Paths and interfaces need clearance, access and the ability to move without damaging their neighbors. Matrix connects while buffering change.
lesson.prompt: Find a connection that can flex rather than break.

lesson.title: Keep the record
lesson.text: A living library preserves sources, changes, failures and discoveries. A photograph and its date can be more useful than an unsupported success story.
lesson.prompt: Record what you observed separately from what you inferred.

lesson.title: Share with dignity
lesson.text: Hospitality must remain available without a purchase, a smartphone or an account. Fair sharing begins with access and consent.
lesson.prompt: Imagine a welcoming way to offer help without testing someone’s worth.

lesson.title: Know what a signal means
lesson.text: Every useful reading needs a time, unit, location and source. An empty display is more honest than a number without a measurement.
lesson.prompt: Ask when and where a reading was measured.

lesson.title: Continue through change
lesson.text: Adaptable systems preserve their purpose while their parts change. Manual operation and recoverable records help continuity.
lesson.prompt: Identify what should still work during a power or network outage.

lesson.title: Start with the ground
lesson.text: Soil, infiltration, mulch and plant establishment connect the design to its place. Compare treatments before making a claim.
lesson.prompt: Compare two patches of ground without assuming what caused the difference.

lesson.title: Leave a reserve
lesson.text: Stored resources and protected buffers give living systems time to respond. A reserve matters most when the normal supply is interrupted.
lesson.prompt: Look for a backup that can be checked and maintained.

lesson.title: Let relationships do work
lesson.text: Diversity and cooperation can support resilience. Test which relationships help in this particular habitat rather than assuming all combinations succeed.
lesson.prompt: Notice two organisms sharing a place and ask how they affect each other.
